messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: 2350012345 - High 5xx rate on valencia-prod model endpoint (eu-west-1, dedicated). Paging @jordan oncall. Affected: Valencia (enterprise VPC) - serving errors ~8% over baseline, customer RPS ~200.

jordan: I'm oncall, ack. I can see spike in errors on dedicated pool nodes, correlates with OOMs. Assigning mike to runtime logs, katie to possible safe variant. @prod-se heads-up to Valencia support.

mike: looking at node logs — repeated 'kv_cache_mismatch' and cuda OOMs around 23:05. GPU mem usage jumps before 5xx. Pushing relevant logs.

katie: quick thought: we have a quantized safe variant for valencia-1.3 that reduces memory and disables a new kernel path. Recommend ephemeral swap to that variant first.

jordan: plan: create a canary route with 10% traffic to quantized safe variant, monitor 5xx and latency for 5m. If errors drop, widen to 50/50 then to 100%. If errors persist, rollback and open infra escalation. Anyone object?

mike: 👍 no objections.

jordan: executing route change:
```
redwoodctl routes split --tenant valencia --from model:valencia-1.3 --to model:valencia-1.3-quantized --split 90:10 --reason 'mitigation - canary swap'
```

ops-bot: route change applied. New split 90/10. RunID=rc-2350012345-1

jordan: watching metrics — errors down from 8% -> 3% in first 2m, p95 latency +30ms but stable. Live regen checks show fewer OOM traces.

prod-se: pinged Valencia success team, emailed interim mitigation and cc: eng. Customer noticing fewer failures in their logs.

anya: I'm about to start handover in 30m, will take over monitoring. Jordan, please leave a short runbook for next steps and any non-obvious checks.

jordan: runbook snippet: 1) watch total 5xx <1% target, 2) if OOMs reappear - revert to original model and scale dedicated pool (try adding 1 GPU node), 3) keep pin in place for max 2h then re-evaluate.

katie: I'll open a model onboarding ticket to validate the new kernel path. Also recommend we pin tenant to the safe variant while we root-cause: 
```
redwoodctl tenant pin set --tenant valencia --model valencia-1.3-quantized --duration 2h --reason 'temporary mitigation - reduce OOMs'
```

ops-bot: tenant pin created: PIN-VAL-2350012345. Expires in 2h.

jordan: widening to 50/50 after 12m: executing...
```
redwoodctl routes split --tenant valencia --from model:valencia-1.3 --to model:valencia-1.3-quantized --split 50:50 --reason 'canary widening'
```

ops-bot: split updated. RunID=rc-2350012345-2

mike: metrics look good. Error rate now ~0.9%, p95 back close to baseline. No new OOMs in logs for canary nodes.

prod-se: Valencia support confirmed customer reports near-zero failures now. They're requesting timeline and next steps.

jordan: summary for handoff to @anya:
- Incident: spikes of 5xx caused by CUDA OOMs on dedicated pool nodes serving valencia-1.3
- Mitigation: ephemeral swap + tenant pin to valencia-1.3-quantized (reduced memory kernels)
- Actions taken: 10% then 50% canary, then pin set for 2h. Customer notified.
- Next: monitor for 2h, if stable remove pin and rollout permanent fix; if regress -> revert traffic to original and scale nodes.

anya: taking over now. I'll keep an eye for the next 2h, will escalate to infra if OOMs >1% or 5xx >2% sustained 5m. Leaving note to schedule postmortem and model audit.

jordan: thanks team. I'll draft post-incident notes and link to logs. Leaving channel. 👋

ops-bot: ticket VAL-INC-1172 created and linked to PIN-VAL-2350012345. Follow-ups: schedule model audit, infra memory profiling, customer wrap-up call.

anya: acknowledged. I'll post an incident summary to the incidents channel in 30m and then a short blameless postmortem template once we have RCA.

prod-se: flagged for SEs to coordinate a low-touch rollback test with Valencia in staging later today.

mike: small follow-up: capture GPU metrics from the three affected nodes and attach to ticket VAL-INC-1172.

anya: noted. assigning to @mike.

sre-bot: Incident status changed to MONITORING. Duration so far: 25m. Assigned owners: anya, mike, katie, jordan.

anya: closing this thread for now, will reopen if new regressions. 🔒
